title: Program. For Example: Dix-Huit Leçons Sur La Société Industrielle (Revision 10)

description.main: The catalogue for Christopher Williams's 2010 exhibition at Bergen Kunsthall, his first solo show in Scandinavia. It gathers his own exhibition press releases with new essays by John Kelsey and Diedrich Diederichsen.
description.extended:
The catalogue for Christopher Williams's 2010 show at Bergen Kunsthall, his first solo presentation in Scandinavia and the tenth revision of his project For Example: Dix-Huit Leçons Sur La Société Industrielle.

The show ran from 15 January to 21 February 2010 and mixed recent photographs with older works. Williams has used the title for a series of exhibitions, each numbered as a new revision. The title proposes a course of lessons on the industrial conditions behind photography. It sets decolonization, industrialization and 1968 beside inventions of the same era that shaped photographic technology. The 80-page softcover was designed by Williams with Petra Hollenbach. It collects for the first time a selection of his press releases for recent exhibitions, which change only slightly from one show to the next. New essays by John Kelsey and Diedrich Diederichsen follow. The cover is laid out as a numbered programme of venue, dates, artist and title.

Williams, born in Los Angeles in 1956, has worked for more than two decades between photography as art and photography used in documentation, advertising and journalism. He has been Professor of Photography at the Kunstakademie Düsseldorf since 2008.
description.artist_bio: Born 1956 in Los Angeles; Professor of Photography at the Kunstakademie Düsseldorf since 2008.
description.exhibition_context: Bergen Kunsthall, 15 January – 21 February 2010; first solo presentation of Williams in Scandinavia.
